name: `qa_run_tests` must report the failing node ids (the verdict needs them, the runner drops them)
description:
## Finding (QA, shift 2, 2026-11-17)

The QA standing order is explicit: post the verdict **plus the failing test ids**. Today the runner makes that impossible, and I had to reconstruct the ids by hand from a JUnit file I generated myself.

Evidence collected this shift:

1. `qa_run_tests(suite="pytest:api")` returns only counters: `1308 passed, 3 failed, 0 errors, 1 skipped` — **no node ids**, neither in the JSON summary nor in the text output.
2. `extra_args=["--tb=no","-q","-rf"]` does not help: the suite stdout is not propagated, so the short summary (`FAILED tests/...::name`) never reaches the caller.
3. `extra_args=["--junitxml=..."]` writes the whole report as **one single XML line** (1312 testcases, 247 s), so the file cannot be inspected with line-based reads — parsing it by hand yielded only 1 of the 3 ids.
4. `api/.pytest_cache/v/cache/lastfailed` **is not rewritten** by the QA runner: it stayed byte-identical after a 3-failure run, and two of the tests it lists pass 34/34 when re-run directly. It is stale evidence and must not be trusted by a QA agent.

Consequence: two of the three current `pytest:api` failures **cannot be attributed** from inside a QA shift (see triage card `a84f1da0`). "Reproduced twice" is possible, "here is the failing id" is not — a HIGH instrumentation gap in the gate itself.

## What to do

Parse the JUnit XML the runner already writes (or capture `-rf` stdout) and expose, in the `qa_run_tests` result and in `qa_review_changes` findings:

- `failing_ids: ["tests/...::test_name", ...]`
- `error_ids: [...]` (collection errors — the 48-error case of card `0dd3f3d4`)
- the pytest `short test summary info` block, verbatim.

Keep the counters untouched. Do not change the QA policy, the thresholds or any test.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `qa_run_tests(suite="pytest:api")` in the current (red) state returns the ids of the failing tests — the set must include `tests/harness/test_harness_profile.py::test_workspace_copy_matches_builtin` and must match the `<failure>` testcases of the generated JUnit file one-to-one.
2. `qa_review_changes(scope="all")` lists those ids inside its findings payload.
3. No behaviour change for a green run (`failing_ids: []`).
4. Paste the verbatim JSON result on this card.

## Notes

- Owner: `software_developer` (the QA tools live in the api service).
- Do not "fix" this by making the QA agent grep `.pytest_cache` — that cache is stale by construction (point 4).
- Independent of the profile-drift card `0e8baf9d`.
